note: The trees every city shares, built by blender/build_trees.py. Nodes are <species>_LOD0..2; colour red is ambient occlusion, green how far the wind moves a vertex, blue a phase for the leaves' flutter. A city picks its mix of species in city.json 'trees'.

plane.note: London plane: the street tree of both cities

gum.note: Eucalyptus: pale bark, open crown in clumps

fig.note: Moreton Bay fig: a broad dark dome on buttresses

jacaranda.note: Jacaranda: purple in late spring (cards swap to the bloom cell with the season)

maple.note: Japanese maple (momiji, Acer palmatum): a low, wide, layered crown; red from mid November in Tokyo and Kyoto

pine.note: Japanese black pine (kuromatsu, Pinus thunbergii): a leaning, crooked trunk under flat pads of needles, as on the Kyoto Gyoen's and the Kokyo Gaien's lawns

sugi.note: Japanese cedar (sugi, Cryptomeria japonica): straight red-brown trunk, a narrow cone; the shrine woods' tree, and stands for hinoki

camphor.note: Camphor laurel (kusunoki, Cinnamomum camphora): a broad, bright evergreen dome on a massive trunk; the shrine trees of Osaka and Kyoto and Meiji Jingu's commonest

zelkova.note: Japanese zelkova (keyaki, Zelkova serrata): a broom of upswept limbs and fine twigs; the avenue tree of Omotesando and the precincts, rust-orange in November

ginkgo.note: Ginkgo (icho, Ginkgo biloba): a tall narrow crown on a central stem; Tokyo's and Osaka's street tree (Midosuji, Jingu Gaien), gold in late November

cherry.note: Somei-yoshino cherry (Cerasus x yedoensis): a short dark trunk that forks low into a few limbs spreading wide, a crown wider than it is tall; pale pink on bare branches for about a fortnight from late March in Tokyo (web/trees.js), then fresh leaves, orange-red in November. Its cards are all bloom cards, shown as the leaf cell out of flower

evergreen.note: Evergreen broadleaf (Schima superba, Machilus; in Japan shii and kashi): a dense, dark, glossy rounded crown; Hong Kong's hillside woods and the laurel forest of the old shrine groves

pisonia.note: Pisonia (Pisonia grandis): several pale soft trunks from one base, leaning out (fallen stems re-root and sprout, so a tree is a clump), and a broad low canopy of big lime-green leaves; the coral cays' forest, mostly 6-8 m on Heron Island

casuarina.note: Coastal she-oak (Casuarina equisetifolia): an open, tapering crown of drooping grey-green branchlets, behind the beaches

shidarezakura.note: Weeping cherry (shidarezakura, Cerasus spachiana 'Pendula', an Edohigan): a stout trunk, scaffold limbs arching up into a dome and curtains of thin branches hanging nearly to the ground, pink a few days before the Somei-yoshino: Maruyama Park's Gion weeping cherry, the temple gardens, Rikugien

kawazu.note: Kawazu-zakura (Cerasus 'Kawazu-zakura', from Kawazu in Izu): a small upright tree whose deep pink flowers open in February, five weeks before the Somei-yoshino's, and last a month

yaezakura.note: Yaezakura (Cerasus serrulata 'Kanzan', the commonest double cherry): upswept limbs in a vase, heavy deep pink double flowers in mid April, about two weeks after the Somei-yoshino, with bronze new leaves

scaevola.note: Beach cabbage (Scaevola taccada): a dense mound of thick yellow-green leaves on many soft stems from the sand, 1-3 m high and wider than tall, the first shrub behind a cay's beach

argusia.note: Octopus bush (Argusia argentea, now Heliotropium arboreum): crooked spreading stems under a rounded crown of silvery grey-green felted leaves in rosettes, about 3.5 m high and 5 m across

tussock.note: Tussock (snow tussock, Chionochloa rigida, and hard tussock, Festuca novae-zelandiae): a dense fountain of fine rolled blades about a metre high, olive at the base and straw to bleached gold above; the grassland of Otago's open hills round Queenstown, and a planted bed's grass

susuki.note: Susuki (Miscanthus sinensis, Japanese silver grass): a clump of broad arching leaves with a pale midrib about 1.2 m high, through which the flowering culms stand to 1.7-2 m with fan-shaped silky heads, red-tinged in late August, silver in October and buff through the winter, when the leaves are straw; the open grass of the Kamo's banks and of Tokyo's park meadows

lomandra.note: Spiny-headed mat-rush (Lomandra longifolia): a dense tussock of stiff, flat, glossy dark green strap leaves 0.6-1 m long, arching but not drooping, with split brown tips; the strappy native of Sydney's sandstone gullies and its planted beds
